Subject: Fwd: Oakwood activation timeline and technical asks — internal scoping

Team — forwarding Oakwood’s ask (see below). Key constraints: Q4 go-live, they want a 48-hour warm-slot reservation and per-tenant KV retention TTL (short-term) to validate PII redaction flows.

My proposal for Product/Eng ask (minimal viable approach):
- Add a per-tenant reservation flag in our routing layer (1 week dev + test) that pins traffic to a reserved Dedicated slot and marks the KV cache as "pinned" for up to N hours.
- Expose a Console toggle/API to set per-tenant retention TTL (defaults: 24/48/72h).
- SRE/ops: run a soft quota to avoid cache exhaustion and add automatic fallback to non-reserved pool if pressure spikes.

Tradeoffs to call out for leadership: cost of reserving capacity versus latency guarantees; extra complexity in autoscaler & billing. Oakwood offered a 12-month reserved commitment if we can deliver pilot guarantees for Q4.

Questions for you all: rough effort estimate for above (eng + SRE + UI), key risk items, and whether this needs an RFC or we can do a focused patch. Monica — can you confirm if CS will own the customer-facing runbook and any support burn?

Wanted to capture discussion before the sync. I’ll book the 30-min slot once I get availability.

— Mina

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: mina.haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, monica.patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, ben.carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Oakwood activation timeline and technical asks — internal scoping

Thanks — this is a good, concrete ask. Quick thoughts from Product/Platform: 

1) Implementation scope: the routing flag + TTL surface is doable as a scoped feature (we can ship a gated Console toggle and API parameter) but we need to be explicit about the guarantees. "Guaranteed warm cache" implies reserved (pre-warmed) GPU slots and warmed KV caches; that’s a non-trivial cost. Minimal approach: offer a documented SLA-like statement for pilot customers (best-effort warm reservation backed by reserved Dedicated capacity for the pilot window).

2) Risks: autoscaler churn, cache eviction pressure for multi-tenant nodes, and billing complexity for per-tenant reservation. We should restrict the pilot to a single region (us-west) and a single model variant to keep scope small.

3) Effort estimate (very rough): Eng (Ben + 2 backend engs) 3–4 weeks to implement routing and TTL plumbing; SRE (Ben) 1 week to extend deployment/process; Console UI (Prod Eng) 1 week for toggle and simple form; QA + runbook ~1 week. Total ~5–6 weeks if we parallelize. If Oakwood needs this before mid-Oct we should treat as a hotpatch and carve out scoped SRE on-call coverage.

4) Next: I recommend a focused RFC to capture billing, fallback behavior, and SLA language, but we can start implementation against an internal feature flag to support the Q4 pilot.

I’ll add a short design sketch and an initial ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RF-4321

— Jordan
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
